finding: A live child of an orphan is neither swept nor killed, yet agent-stop answers stopped true.
why: kin keeps only a pool process whose parent ended, so the orphan's own child is skipped; kill_tree adds `extra` without expanding its descendants, and survivors is computed from members only.
fix: After selecting the orphans, expand each into its live descendants before killing, or count a pool process whose parent is itself an orphan as an orphan.
evidence: `if not _parent_ended(member, parents, pool, msys): continue` (process.py:301-302); `members += [m for m in extra if m not in members]` (process.py:350)

finding: When Git's `ps` is missing or fails, the sweep treats every MSYS process with a gone Windows parent as an orphan, without reporting a gap.
why: `_msys_parents` returns {} on failure, so `msys.get(pid) is None` is True for all of them, and a live MSYS child of the caller newer than the root can be killed.
fix: Have `_msys_parents` report failure, and in kin treat an MSYS-ambiguous process as a gap, not as an orphan.
evidence: `except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError): return {}` (process.py:118-119) and `return msys.get(pid) is None` (process.py:181).

finding: No test reads the console helper's second output line or its access-denied and failure branches, so the 'could not be read' honesty path on Windows is unproven end to end.
why: The incomplete-search test replaces `_console_peers` wholesale with a canned gap, and the live runs only show the no-gap case; a broken `unread` line parse, a wrong `get_last_error() == 5` check, or the exit-code and exception branches would all pass, letting agent-stop answer `stopped` true with an unread console.
fix: Add a Windows-gated test that monkeypatches `subprocess.run` inside `_console_peers` to return stdout like `'11 12\n7\n'`, a non-zero return code, and a raised OSError, asserting the ids and the gap text for each.
evidence: process.py:166-171 `if done.returncode != 0: return [], f"the console lists could not be read (exit ...)"` / `found, unread = (done.stdout.splitlines() + ["", ""])[:2]` / `gap = f"the consoles of processes {ids} could not be read" if ids else None`; test line 811 `lambda pids: ([], "the console lists could not be read (x)")`

finding: A pool member whose creation time cannot be read, with a live Windows parent id, is dropped from the sweep with no gap reported.
why: `_parent_ended` returns False on `mine is None` before the later `born is None` path that feeds `unknown`.
fix: Return None from `_parent_ended` for an unreadable creation time and add that pid to the gap list in kin.
evidence: `if mine is None or theirs is None or theirs <= mine: return False` (process.py:179)

criterion: empty/missing inputs; safety (can the sweep kill a process that is not the agent's)
finding: A process missing from the process listing, or an empty listing, counts as 'parent ended' instead of 'unknown'
why: `parents` is read before the console read; a process that appeared in between, or every peer when `_parents()` returns {}, has `parents.get(pid)` None, so _parent_ended returns True and a newer one is killed even though its parent is live; none of these cases reports a gap.
fix: Read `parents` after `_console_peers`, skip any pool member absent from `parents`, and return a gap when `_parents()` or `_msys_parents()` came back empty.

finding: Unit test named 'never the caller or an ancestor' never puts an ancestor of the caller or of the root in the swept pool.
why: Deleting the `line(os.getpid())` or `line(pid)` exclusion at process.py:300 (keeping only the pid itself) leaves this test green, because 996 (the caller's parent) is not a key in `parents` and 10 (the root's parent) is dropped by the age check (start 1 < 50), so the caller's ancestor, the safety item the brief asks about, is unpinned.
fix: Add a pool member that is the caller's parent (or grandparent), is newer than the root and has a parent outside the pool, and assert it is not in `found`.
evidence: parents = {10: 1, 100: 10, 101: 100, 300: 996, 400: 999, ...}; started = {10: 1, 100: 50, ...}; process.py:300 `for member in pool - set(members) - line(os.getpid()) - line(pid):`

finding: The Windows `_parent_ended` rule that a parent id held by a newer process counts as ended is never exercised.
why: The only parent-in-table case is 500, whose parent 300 is older, so changing `theirs <= mine` at process.py:179 to always return False, or dropping the reused-id test, keeps every test green on both platforms; the live-MSYS-parent branch (`msys.get(pid) is None`) has no unit case either.
fix: Add a Windows-gated unit case with an orphan whose parent id exists in `parents` but was created after it (expect found), and one whose MSYS parent is live (expect spared), via the patched `_created` and `_msys_parents`.
evidence: process.py:177-181 `if parent in parents and parent != pid: mine, theirs = _created(pid), _created(parent); if mine is None or theirs is None or theirs <= mine: return False` / `return msys.get(pid) is None`; test patches `_msys_parents` to `{}` and uses only started = {..., 500: 90} under parent 300 = 70

finding: No test covers an orphan that has its own live child.
why: The live ORPHAN script and the kin table use only leaf orphans.
fix: Add a case with an orphan plus a child of that orphan in the console or session, and assert both die.

finding: The Windows `_parent_ended` takes a `peers` parameter it never uses.
fix: Drop it from the Windows variant or pass the shared pool through a common helper.
evidence: `def _parent_ended(pid: int, parents: dict[int, int], peers: set[int],` with no use of `peers` in its body

finding: Three start-time helpers with overlapping names (`creation_time`, `_created`, `_started`), and POSIX `_started` re-parses the /proc stat field that `creation_time` already parses
why: The same rule lives in two places and the names do not say how they differ.
fix: Factor one `_start_ticks(pid)` reader used by both.

finding: `extra: list[int] = ()` annotates a list but defaults to a tuple
why: The annotation and default disagree, and `extra` does not say that these processes are swept orphans.
fix: Annotate `Sequence[int]` and state in the docstring what `extra` holds.

finding: `alive` is patched to always True, so the 'unreadable start time of a dead process raises no gap' branch is untested.
why: Removing the `if alive(member)` guard at process.py:305 leaves the test green, though it would make every reaped orphan with no readable start time turn a clean stop into `stopped` false.
fix: Add a second unreadable-start orphan with `alive` False for that id and assert it is not named in `gap`.
evidence: monkeypatch.setattr(process, "alive", lambda pid: True); process.py:304-306 `if born is None: if alive(member): unknown.append(str(member))`
